subtitle: When you have caused harm, own the specific action, offer a change that fits and listen to the person’s response, without claiming that everything has been repaired.
scope: All people, ages, words, notes, replies and encounters are original example; no actual personnel or demographic record is involved. The main review exchange, garden-and-model-railway encounter and explicit supervisor example retain distinct scopes. No clinical diagnosis, permanent motive or sincerity verdict, cultural orientation, real complaint finding, release approval or guaranteed repair is supplied. Practice wording is not an approved agency statement, legal admission procedure or exception to actual duties, information arrangements and assigned procedures. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the person or area responsible within ADSA.
introTranscript: Read a complete original exchange about an unchecked draft field and an age-based judgment. Compare apology openings, keep an explanation from becoming an excuse and propose a specific change within the actual role. Receive two personally learned meanings of repair, then keep a recipient’s boundary and the supervisor’s actual duty distinct. Review the performed apology and limited feedback honestly. Use the full example or private unrecorded learning at your own pace; no real apology, confession or forgiveness is required.

lessons.title: Name the action rather than blame the response
lessons.summary: An apology can own a specific supplied action without making the recipient’s reaction the error or declaring a formal finding.
lessons.objective: Identify the action and recipient’s account in the full exchange in the example.
objectives: Identify the action and recipient’s account in the full exchange in the example.
Distinguish ownership of a stated action from blame shifted to the recipient.
Choose an opening apology that stays within the supplied facts.
takeaways: Name what you said or did at its actual scope.
An account of your intention does not erase the other person’s supplied experience.
Owning a practice action is not a clinical diagnosis or a completed policy investigation.
lessons.statement: Begin with your actual action instead of making the other person’s response the problem.

intro.heading: Read the exchange before selecting the apology
intro.body:
In original practice DHS practice, Silas and Mei discuss a proposed internal review note. Mei is explicitly a thirty-eight-year-old adult in this example; no actual demographic or personnel record is involved. The complete practice note says: “Examples checked. Contact field not checked.” Mei asks who will examine the contact field. Silas replies, “Someone your age should not lead this review.” Mei says, “The age comment dismissed my contribution. I asked who will examine the unchecked field.” No actual appointment, investigation finding, operational approval or later result is supplied.

Silas considers an opening that says, “I am sorry you took my concern the wrong way.” That sentence places the error in Mei’s interpretation rather than identifying Silas’s age-based remark. It also leaves the concrete review question displaced. The example supplies Silas’s words and Mei’s account, so the apology can start with those facts: he made the remark about age, and Mei described it as dismissing a contribution. It does not need to make Mei prove every earlier experience or accept Silas’s explanation first.

An alternative proposed opening says, “I said someone your age should not lead the review. I am sorry for making that age-based judgment about your contribution.” This is original practice wording, not an approved agency statement or a legal admission procedure. It names the supplied action instead of claiming a permanent psychological motive or deciding the merits of an actual complaint. Silas can acknowledge a specific remark while actual roles and formal responsibilities keep their own processes.

Silas’s intended concern, if offered, would be a different kind of information from the words and their received meaning. No intention statement is supplied at this point. Inventing one would not make the apology more truthful. If he later explains a reason, it should not become a demand that Mei dismiss her account or agree the remark was harmless. An explanation can be examined while ownership of the action remains clear.

The contact field also matters. Mei did not ask for an assessment of age; the contribution concerned an unchecked part of the draft. A responsible response should not make that task question a reward for accepting an apology. The example supplies neither a final draft owner decision nor a guarantee that the field can be checked immediately by Silas. The course will develop a fitting proposed action without inventing those authorities or results.

Privately compare the two apology openings and describe where each places responsibility. You may work with the full example without confessing an actual incident, deciding a real allegation or publicly identifying a person. Recognizing what an opening owns is useful personal understanding, even when no live apology or operational outcome follows.

lessons.keyStatement: A truthful opening owns the stated action without writing the recipient’s answer.

items.title: Own a specific action
items.body: Silas’s proposed apology repeats what he said and identifies the age-based judgment about a contribution. That gives Mei an account of the action being acknowledged instead of requiring her to infer it from a vague regret. It does not establish every earlier event, a lasting motive or a formal finding. The scope stays with the supplied remark.

items.title: Do not turn the recipient into the error
items.body: The “took it wrong” opening makes Mei’s interpretation the thing being apologized for. In the example, Mei has described the contribution that was dismissed. Receiving that account lets Silas examine his remark rather than asking Mei to prove why she should be heard. Ownership does not require declaring every future interpretation settled or taking over an actual process.

items.title: Keep the contribution available
items.body: Mei’s question concerns an unchecked field, not an invitation to judge ability from age. Naming the action should help return to that contribution without bargaining for forgiveness. Acknowledging the wrong focus does not give Silas draft-release or personnel authority; the actual next task follows its appropriate role and evidence. No result is created by the opening alone.

tabs.label: Sorry for your interpretation
tabs.body: Silas says he is sorry Mei took the remark incorrectly. The sentence does not acknowledge the age-based judgment and makes her supplied response the problem. Mei’s actual task question remains unanswered. A more responsible opening names the particular words and their received effect without asking her to agree to a new account of her own reaction. It need not claim knowledge of every motive or history.

tabs.label: Sorry for every imaginable event
tabs.body: Silas admits to unspecified past conduct, diagnoses his permanent character and promises that the entire situation is resolved. The example provides neither those events nor that outcome. An apology can be specific and accountable without inventing facts, a diagnosis or the result of an assigned process. Stay with what is supplied and keep later responsibilities distinct.

tabs.label: Sorry for the action actually supplied
tabs.body: Silas proposes naming the remark about age and apologizing for that judgment about Mei’s contribution. This owns the action and receives her supplied account without making forgiveness a condition. The statement remains practice wording, not an approved operational statement or completed finding. Its acceptance and any fitting task change require their own answers and actual roles.

check.question: Which opening best owns the supplied action?
check.correct: “I said someone your age should not lead the review. I am sorry for making that age-based judgment about your contribution.”
wrong: “I am sorry you took my concern the wrong way.”
“This proves every imagined past event occurred and the investigation is complete.”
“I will acknowledge the remark only if you first forgive me.”
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The opening names the supplied action without shifting responsibility or requiring a recipient’s answer.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The “took it wrong” wording makes the reaction the error rather than owning the age-based remark. The course supplies no unspecified past events or completed investigation. Forgiveness cannot be required before a person names an action or considers a response.

lessons.title: Keep an explanation from becoming an excuse
lessons.summary: A stated intention can help explain an account, but it cannot erase the action, overwrite the received meaning or require the recipient to provide reassurance.
lessons.objective: Distinguish Silas’s newly supplied intention statement from his action and Mei’s account.
objectives: Distinguish Silas’s newly supplied intention statement from his action and Mei’s account.

takeaways: Intention, action and received meaning are different information.
Explaining a reason should not place the responsibility back on the recipient.
A listener is not required to certify the apologizer’s character before the task or actual process continues.
lessons.statement: Explain your reason at its scope without making it an instruction to forget the action.

intro.heading: An intention account can add information without rewriting the exchange
intro.body:
Silas now offers an explanation. He says, “I was worried about whether the unchecked field had enough context, but I used age as a shortcut.” This is his stated account, not an independently verified motive or a claim about every earlier interaction. The age-based words and Mei’s response remain supplied facts. A purpose concerning draft context does not make age evidence of whether a particular field has been examined.

Silas first considers adding, “So you should not feel dismissed, and you should tell the group I am fair.” That addition would use the explanation to cancel Mei’s account and obtain a character certificate. It changes the focus from owning an action to asking the recipient to relieve the apologizer’s discomfort. Mei’s contribution should not depend on saying the words were harmless or publicly defending Silas.

A more responsible proposed continuation keeps the distinction: “My concern was the field’s context, and I used an age-based shortcut instead of asking about the field. That does not make the remark appropriate. I will address the review question through the relevant task information.” This is practice wording. It does not give Silas a new assignment, authority to change personnel decisions or proof of lasting impartiality. It names the difference between the intended question and the action used to pursue it.

The distinction helps a learner avoid two extremes. It would be inaccurate to treat a newly supplied intention as proof that no effect could occur. It would also be inaccurate to invent a permanent intention that Silas never supplied. A reply can receive the stated reason without granting it the power to erase the action or decide a formal investigation. The person receiving an apology can have a different view of its fit; the course does not require agreement as its ending.

Explanation also has timing and choice limits. Silas does not need to deliver an extended autobiography, ask Mei to become his coach or demand a private discussion. If Mei does not want that conversation, it is not proof that she refuses the task, misrepresents the action or owes a new opportunity. Actual information and assigned process responsibilities still have their own routes, while a personal explanation remains a separate proposed exchange.

Privately identify the intention, action and received meaning in this complete fiction. Then explain how a short continuation could retain all three without demanding reassurance. You do not need to diagnose anyone’s character or produce a public demonstration of apology. The learning gain is a more truthful account of why an explanation can be useful and why it does not provide complete repair by itself.

Keep the action and Mei’s account alongside it.
Compare explanation with cancellation or reassurance demands.
Leave the recipient’s response and actual procedures separate.
lessons.keyStatement: A reason can add context; it does not erase an owned action or supply a forgiveness result.

flashcards.back: Silas says he worried about context and used age as a shortcut.
The intention statement does not change the age-based words already supplied.
Mei’s account of a dismissed contribution remains her supplied response.
The explanation is used to say no concern exists or the recipient must defend the apologizer.
Retain ownership and return to relevant task information without demanding reassurance.

items.title: Hear the supplied reason at its scope
items.body: Silas’s reason adds a particular account of what he was thinking. It does not verify every motive or decide how Mei must experience the words. Retaining “Silas says” keeps its origin clear. A responsible apology can name that reason briefly while continuing to own the age-based shortcut instead of claiming the intention settles every question.

items.title: Do not turn explanation into cancellation
items.body: The requested field context and the age remark are different things. A genuine context question could be asked through the draft information without an age judgment. Saying the remark was harmless because the question mattered would erase the very distinction the explanation reveals. The proposed continuation should acknowledge the shortcut rather than make the recipient accept it as necessary.

items.title: Do not demand a character certificate
items.body: Silas’s proposed request that Mei tell the group he is fair asks her to supply reassurance rather than receive a changed action. It also makes the task contribution conditional on public agreement. A person can offer a responsible account without obtaining a permanent character rating, compulsory coaching conversation or statement that an actual policy concern no longer exists.

tabs.heading: Compare uses of the same explanation

tabs.label: The reason proves there was no concern
tabs.body: Silas points to his worry about context and says it means Mei could not reasonably feel dismissed. That makes the intention account override the supplied response. It also misses the relevant distinction: field context should be examined through task information, not presumed age-based ability. The reason can be retained without becoming proof of harmlessness or a completed finding.

tabs.label: The recipient must reassure the speaker
tabs.body: Silas explains his worry, then asks Mei to describe him as fair before anyone continues. This makes the apology into a request for a public character certificate and places new work on the recipient. The field question and actual process should not depend on that certificate. Naming the action and possible change is a more fitting contribution than requiring the listener to relieve the speaker’s discomfort.

tabs.label: The explanation keeps ownership
tabs.body: Silas says he worried about the field and used an age-based shortcut instead of asking about its context. He retains the action and proposes using relevant information. This explains what could change without claiming permission, a permanent motive verdict or Mei’s forgiveness. The account can remain truthful even if Mei does not want a personal conversation or offers a different response.

check.question: Which use of Silas’s explanation is responsible?
check.correct: Keep his stated concern alongside ownership of the age-based shortcut and use relevant task information without requiring Mei to reassure or forgive him.
wrong: Use his stated intention to prove Mei’s account is false.
Require Mei to tell the group Silas is permanently fair before continuing.
Invent an unsupplied lasting motive and use it as a completed finding.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The explanation adds context without replacing the action, recipient’s account or actual roles.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A stated intention cannot make the supplied response false. Reassurance is not the recipient’s price for contributing to the task. An unsupplied lasting motive is an invention, and neither an explanation nor a course determines an actual finding.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain a reason without using it to erase the action or demand reassurance.

move.control: A reason and responsibility can coexist in a truthful apology.
move.failure: The explanation cancels the recipient’s account, invents a lasting motive or makes forgiveness a gate.

lessons.title: Offer a specific change within the actual role
lessons.summary: A possible repair should address the action and the task without promising authority, approval or restored trust that the example does not supply.
lessons.objective: Describe a proposed change that addresses the age shortcut and unchecked-field question.
objectives: Describe a proposed change that addresses the age shortcut and unchecked-field question.
Distinguish an offer from performed repair, accepted apology and restored trust.
Choose an accurate draft account without claiming a completed field review.
takeaways: An offer should have a specific connection to the action and the relevant task.
Words, performed action and a recipient’s response are different evidence.
Research about perceived apologies does not guarantee a real relationship result or prescribe an agency procedure.
lessons.statement: Make the proposed change understandable and keep its performance and result open.

intro.heading: Connect the apology to something that can actually be examined
intro.body:
Silas now considers what a possible change would involve. The original note still says the examples are checked and the contact field is not checked. No actual draft owner, approved assignment, completed examination or release decision is supplied. Silas can propose considering the field’s actual content instead of treating age as evidence of ability, and asking the appropriate draft owner who will examine the unchecked field. That is a proposed contribution, not proof that the field has been reviewed or that Mei is appointed to lead a real task.

The original 2016 Lewicki, Polin and Lount study examines how participants perceived different apology statements and components in hypothetical trust-violation scenarios. It treats responsibility and repair offers as distinguishable content. Its design and discussion do not supply a guarantee of actual trust restoration in a continuing workplace relationship. The course therefore uses the distinction between a statement and its proposed action, not a required component count, a psychological score or a promise that a certain apology will obtain forgiveness.

Silas’s proposed action might be worded: “I will consider the review question through the relevant field information rather than age. I can ask the appropriate draft owner about the unchecked contact field.” This keeps the intended change specific. It does not promise authority that the example has not supplied. The proposal is also different from saying, “I will approve the whole page today,” which would substitute a release guarantee for examining the unanswered question.

A more accurate proposed draft account would retain “Examples checked. Contact field awaits appropriate review.” The revision is practice wording, not an approved release or supplied examination. It describes what is known and what still needs an actual role and result. Changing the sentence does not itself change the underlying field status. That distinction helps Silas avoid repairing an uncomfortable conversation with another unsupported claim.

Mei is not responsible for designing every change, coaching Silas indefinitely or accepting an apology before the task question is considered. An offer can leave a fitting answer possible without delegating the apologizer’s responsibility back to the recipient. If the appropriate actual process calls for other information or action, that process retains its role. The course does not decide personnel assignments, authorize a public promise or certify complete repair.

Privately describe one possible change, what it addresses and what evidence would be needed to say it happened. You can retain a meaningful proposed action while its actual performance and outcome remain unknown. A useful apology is not measured by how many parts a learner can recite or how much certainty a sentence claims. It becomes more understandable when the action, actual role and missing result are distinguished.

accordion.heading: Make the offered change useful and honest

items.title: Address the shortcut rather than offer a reward
items.body: The proposed change returns the review question to relevant information. Offering Mei an unrelated benefit in exchange for silence would not examine the age-based judgment and could obstruct an actual concern. A fitting action should have an understandable connection to the supplied problem, with the actual roles and recipient’s response left intact.

items.title: Do not promise another role’s outcome
items.body: Silas can propose asking the appropriate draft owner about the field. The example does not give him authority to appoint a leader, approve the page or guarantee a deadline. An apology should not gain apparent strength by inventing those powers. Describe the offered action and the actual condition that would need clarification, rather than promise a result someone else must authorize or provide.

items.title: Retain the difference between words and evidence
items.body: Writing that the contact field awaits review is an accurate proposal, not proof the field has changed. A later account would need evidence of the actual examination and decision. Likewise, a research participant’s rating of an apology statement is not a real colleague’s forgiveness. Keep the particular kind of evidence visible so that a promising sentence does not become an invented outcome.

tabs.label: A guarantee of immediate approval
tabs.body: Silas promises the entire page will be approved immediately as proof that he is sorry. The supplied note contains an unchecked field and no release authority. The promise neither answers who will examine it nor establishes an actual review. A more fitting contribution identifies the field question and its responsible role instead of treating a powerful-sounding promise as performed repair.

tabs.label: A reward for silence
tabs.body: Silas offers an unrelated advantage if Mei agrees not to raise the age concern. This turns an apology into a bargain that obstructs a concern instead of owning the action. The field contribution and actual reporting should not depend on silence or forgiveness. A responsible proposed change keeps its task relevance and actual procedures without purchasing a particular personal response.

tabs.label: A specific action with honest status
tabs.body: Silas proposes using field information rather than age and asking the appropriate draft owner about the unchecked contact field. The revised practice note leaves that review open. The contribution has a reason connected to the action without claiming assignment, approval or restored trust. Performance, the recipient’s answer and later effects each need their own evidence.

check.question: Which proposed change fits the supplied situation?
check.correct: Consider the question through field information rather than age and clarify the appropriate field-review role without claiming the review or approval is complete.
wrong: Promise immediate page approval despite an unchecked field and absent release authority.
Offer an unrelated reward on condition that Mei does not report.
Treat the revised note as proof that the field has been examined and trust restored.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The offer connects to the supplied action and task while leaving actual role and result questions intact.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An apology does not create release authority or erase an unchecked field. A reward conditioned on silence does not own the action and can obstruct a concern. Revised wording is not the underlying examination or the recipient’s restored trust; those results are not supplied.

intro.heading: Follow an original garden and model-railway encounter
intro.body:
In a separate conversation, Petra has omitted Naima’s and Ewan’s contributions from a neighborhood project note. The example concerns that omitted credit, not an actual DHS record or legal process. Petra wants to apologize and proposes a quick conversation that says, “Sorry about the missing names.” Naima asks Petra to consider a practical shared task as part of the response; Ewan asks Petra to specify the missing contribution accurately in a written correction. Petra initially calls Naima avoidance of the apology and Ewan distrustful formality.

Naima chooses to explain a meaning learned in a family garden group. When someone left another person’s watering task undone, returning together for the next needed task could express taking responsibility for the shared care. Words mattered, but doing something connected to the omission kept an apology from being detached from the activity. Naima’s account does not say an action makes every apology sufficient or that Petra may decide another person’s schedule without asking.

Ewan chooses to explain a meaning learned in a childhood model-railway group. A mistaken description of someone’s design contribution was corrected by identifying the detail and checking that the new description matched what was actually built. Ewan learned precise acknowledgment as care for the contribution, not simply a demand for formal language. The account does not authorize publication of every name or require Petra to produce a complete history before a small correction can be considered.

The offered accounts widen Petra’s judgments. Naima’s practical proposal can express responsibility rather than avoidance of words. Ewan’s request for specificity can express care rather than distrust. Petra can now propose naming the omitted contributions accurately and asking whether a relevant chosen practical task would also fit. This changes the response for received reasons instead of assuming that one verbal form is the only sincere apology or that every different form should be added compulsorily.

Fit, the exact corrected detail, scheduling, willingness and any publication remain open. Petra must not call the proposal accepted merely because the meanings were explained. Neither Naima nor Ewan represents every gardener, hobby participant, family or age group. No personal developmental rank, permanent style or psychological sincerity assessment follows. The separate personal learning also does not make Silas’s main age-based remark acceptable or delay the actual supervisor responsibility.

Privately explain how Petra’s interpretation changed and one proposed response it could inform. You can value the wider understanding without holding a neighborhood event, disclosing your own experience or making someone accept a particular repair. A different meaning is not automatically an excuse; receiving it helps make the next offer more attentive while accuracy and actual requirements remain.

flashcards.back: A relevant shared task connects responsibility with continuing garden care.

accordion.heading: Trace offered meaning to a changed response

items.title: Receive practical care as a particular meaning
items.body: Naima’s garden account gives a practical task a reason beyond substituting action for an apology. It connects responsibility to the shared activity affected by the omission. Petra can receive that reason without appointing Naima to another task or claiming that action alone satisfies every person. The next proposal should leave willingness and feasibility possible rather than become a compulsory performance.

items.title: Receive precision as care for contribution
items.body: Ewan’s railway account explains why naming the correct detail matters. Petra’s distrust judgment overlooked that care for what was actually contributed. A precise acknowledgment should still be accurate and handled through its actual conditions; the personal account does not publish a name or establish every detail. Receiving the meaning strengthens a fitting question instead of creating automatic certainty.

items.title: Offer a change without combining every preference by force
items.body: Petra can propose accurate credit and consideration of a relevant chosen task because the accounts explained acknowledgment and responsibility differently. That is not a requirement that everyone receive both forms or a guarantee of sincerity. Another reply may change the proposal. Private learning can retain the wider interpretation before any corrected note or activity exists.

tabs.heading: Compare interpretations of a repair request

tabs.label: The preferred form proves insincerity
tabs.body: Petra calls Naima evasive and Ewan distrustful because neither request matches the quick conversation. Their chosen accounts supply reasons related to responsibility and care for contribution. Those reasons widen the motive judgments without certifying every action or predicting a group. Petra can explain what she now understands and make a new offer instead of treating her familiar form as a sincerity test.

tabs.label: Learning becomes compulsory repair
tabs.body: Petra requires everyone to take part in a practical task and publish a detailed written account. Understanding the meanings has not supplied agreement, scheduling, corrected facts or publication permission. A forced combination could remove the choice that makes the response fitting. An offered change should keep the particular reasons and actual conditions visible rather than convert them into a mandatory procedure.

tabs.label: The offer changes through received reasons
tabs.body: Petra proposes naming the missing contributions accurately and asks whether a relevant chosen shared task also fits. The proposal reflects Ewan’s precise acknowledgment and Naima’s continuing-care account without inferring a demographic preference. Its acceptance, details and performance remain unknown. The learning can be meaningful while a public note or actual activity has not occurred.

intro.heading: Keep the person’s boundary and the actual responsibility together
intro.body:
The example now supplies Mei’s answer to a possible further personal conversation: “I want the contact field checked. I am not ready to talk personally about the remark.” This is a specific boundary and task need. It is not a supplied declaration that Silas is permanently unforgivable, a refusal to contribute, a complete acceptance of his apology or a policy finding. Silas should retain the actual words rather than fill them with the response he hoped for or feared.

Silas considers asking repeatedly until Mei agrees to the personal conversation. That would make his wish for reassurance more important than the answer actually given. He can acknowledge that Mei does not want that discussion now and keep the task question visible through appropriate roles. Doing so does not authorize him to stop assigned work, isolate Mei, publish the concern or decide that no formal process can occur. The course supplies no new confidentiality promise or permission to disregard actual procedures.

In a separate original responsibility example connected to the exchange, supervisor Paola receives the age-related allegation. Mei’s adult age is expressly supplied in the example, rather than inferred from appearance or a name. Under actual MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow the applicable agency complaint/investigation procedures or Affirmative Action Plan. Neither Silas’s apology nor Mei’s preference about a personal conversation delays that duty.

The report is not an investigation finding. Actual assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain. The course does not assign every ordinary staff observer the identical manager responsibility, and employees have encouraged reporting routes. Paola should not require an accepted apology, a particular course term, chart proof or consultant agreement before the actual supervisor step. Equally, following that step does not make Mei consent to an optional public account or personal coaching conversation.

Silas’s conduct after the boundary is part of whether the proposed change is actually pursued. It would be inconsistent to say he owns the age shortcut and then treat Mei’s declined personal discussion as evidence that her task question need not be received. A truthful next response can keep the field question separate from the personal conversation, identify the relevant actual role and avoid retaliatory obstruction. It cannot promise a field result the example has not supplied or decide an allegation outside actual assigned procedures.

Privately explain Mei’s answer, one unsupported interpretation of it and Paola’s required next step. Learning does not require making a real apology, forgiving someone or recounting an actual complaint. The exercise helps distinguish an offered repair, a chosen personal response and an actual process so that none is treated as permission to erase the others.

items.title: Retain responsibility without bargaining
items.body: The apology should not require Mei to forgive before Silas considers the actual field question. Nor should Paola wait for forgiveness before her immediate supervisor report. intro.heading: Close with the action performed and the answer received
intro.body:
The closing example supplies an apology that Silas actually speaks: “I said someone your age should not lead the review. I am sorry for making that age-based judgment about your contribution. I will consider the field question through relevant information rather than age, and I can ask the appropriate draft owner about the unchecked contact field.” Mei replies, “That identifies the remark. I still want the field question addressed, and I am not ready for a personal discussion.” These are original practice statements, not an approved actual agency communication or a clinical measure.

The reply gives Silas particular feedback. Mei recognizes that the action has been identified; she retains the task need and personal boundary. It does not establish forgiveness, complete acceptance, restored trust or the completion of every needed response. Silas should not turn “identifies the remark” into permission to publish an apology story or proof that the concern no longer matters. The continuation she does not want remains a personal discussion, not the task question she explicitly raised.

Silas has also drafted a proposed status sentence that preserves the examples checked and the contact field awaiting appropriate review. No owner reply, completed field examination, actual assignment or page release is supplied. A changed account and a proposed task follow-up are meaningful progress in reasoning, but they do not make the underlying review complete. The next actual result must come through its fitting evidence and role rather than being inferred from the apology.

In the separate supervisor example, the example supplies that Paola immediately reports the allegation to the agency Affirmative Action Officer. No investigation finding or disciplinary result is supplied. That step can be accurately described as performed without being renamed complete resolution. Assigned procedures and nonretaliation retain their roles. The course does not certify any actual complaint, and Silas’s apology neither causes a required report to disappear nor decides its merits.

The personal garden-and-model-railway encounter retains its different learning gain. Petra widens avoidance and distrust judgments after receiving shared practical care and precise contribution acknowledgment meanings. Her proposed offer changes, but acceptance, scheduling, corrected details and publication remain open. Personal understanding can be valuable before a public note or actual task exists. No individual cultural orientation or permanent sincerity certificate follows from that reflection.

Privately explain what Silas said, what Mei’s reply supports and which results are still missing. You can continue with the whole example or relevant actual work through its responsibilities without a compulsory live apology, public confession or fixed personal repair timetable. The close values a specific accountable action while keeping its relationship, task and process limits honest.

items.title: Continue from the relevant question

This contradicts the closing example’s performed statements and report. Unknown later effects do not erase known actions, nor do they prove failure. Retain what was performed and what remains open as different evidence rather than require a complete victory to recognize a learning gain.

tabs.label: The action and answer retain their scope
tabs.body: Silas records the apology, Mei’s recognition of its specific identification, the continuing field question and personal boundary. Paola’s report stays a distinct performed step without a finding. Petra’s changed understanding stays personal rather than a task result. This close preserves meaningful progress without inventing forgiveness, trust, release or a permanent sincerity certificate.

jobAid.title: Offer an accountable apology without taking over the answer
jobAid.subtitle: Keep the action, the proposed change, the recipient’s response and actual process results distinct.

sections.heading: Name the supplied action
items: The full practice note says examples checked and contact field not checked. Mei asks about that field; Silas makes an age-based leadership judgment; Mei describes a dismissed contribution. No actual appointment, finding or release is supplied.

Name the specific remark and apologize for that judgment about the contribution. “You took it wrong” moves the error to the recipient’s response, while invented histories or permanent motive verdicts add unsupported information.
A practice opening is not an actual agency-approved communication or legal admission procedure. Learning does not require a confession, public personal certificate or an actual complaint.

sections.heading: Explain without canceling responsibility
items: Silas says he worried about the field context and used age as a shortcut. Keep his stated intention, the words and Mei’s account as different information rather than make one erase the others.
A context question should be examined through relevant information, not presumed age-based ability. A stated reason does not require the recipient to withdraw a concern or certify permanent fairness.
Do not make a personal coaching conversation, reassurance or forgiveness the price of receiving the task contribution. The supplied boundary and actual roles keep their own meanings.

sections.heading: Make an offer specific and honest
items: Propose considering the field information rather than age and asking the appropriate draft owner about the unchecked field. No release, appointment, deadline authority or completed examination is supplied by the apology.
Retain the examples checked and the contact field awaiting appropriate review in proposed wording. Changing that sentence does not perform the review or establish restored trust.

Hypothetical apology-perception research does not create an agency-required component count or guarantee a person’s response. A proposed repair, its performance and its effect each need their own evidence.

sections.heading: Receive personally learned repair meanings
items: Naima connects a relevant shared task with responsibility learned in family garden care. Ewan connects a precise correction with care for a contribution learned in a model-railway group. These chosen accounts widen Petra’s avoidance and distrust judgments.

Petra proposes accurate contribution acknowledgment and asks whether a relevant chosen task fits. The response changes for received reasons; accuracy, willingness, schedule, publication and performance remain open.
A meaning is not a fixed group style, personal sincerity rank, compulsory story or an excuse for the main age-based action. Private understanding can be valuable without a public note or activity.

sections.heading: Keep the answer and actual responsibility together
items: Mei wants the field checked and is not ready for a personal discussion. That answer is neither forgiveness nor refusal of all task participation. Do not pressure a different answer or turn the boundary into exclusion.

Supervisor Paola immediately reports all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or agency Affirmative Action Officer and follows actual complaint/investigation procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. Apology, forgiveness, vocabulary, course or consultant approval cannot gate that duty. Reporting is not a finding; actual assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain.

In the closing example, Silas speaks the apology, Mei recognizes identification of the remark and retains the task need and boundary, and Paola reports to agency AAO. Field examination, release, forgiveness, restored trust and investigation findings remain unknown.

The consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their work. Retain appropriate ADSA referral for excluded Native American- and Tribal-specific matters.

remember: Own the action without blaming the response or inventing an unsupplied history.
Offer a fitting change without a forgiveness bargain or authority guarantee.
Retain the performed words, actual answer and missing results separately.

sources.title: Lewicki, Polin and Lount: An Exploration of the Structure of Effective Apologies
sources.note: The original 2016 study distinguishes content in apology statements and participants’ perceptions in hypothetical scenarios. It supports examining a responsibility statement and a repair offer as different content, not a required formula or guarantee of forgiveness, actual action or restored trust.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Retains actual protected-class standards, encouraged reporting routes, immediate manager and supervisor reports through HR or agency Affirmative Action Officer, assigned procedures and nonretaliation. An apology or declined personal conversation is not a reporting exception or an investigation finding.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Supports receiving personalized learned meanings and changing a response. The separate garden and model-railway accounts widen sincerity judgments without creating fixed group styles, compulsory stories or an excuse for the main action.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Explains daily equity responsibilities and the tools and roles for qualifying formal analysis. Practicing an apology does not complete analysis, grant approval authority or demonstrate an operational outcome.

sources.title: DHS: Content and writing guidelines
sources.note: Supports an accurate account of the action, recipient’s reply, proposed follow-up and missing result. A revised note is not a completed field review, and a particular acknowledgment is not complete repair.
